humanities_role_explanation: MMMU-Pro is a general multi-discipline college-level benchmark (30 subjects, six disciplines); humanities subjects (Art, Art Theory, Design, Music, History, Literature, Sociology, Psychology) merely supply a subset of items while the competence tested is general multimodal understanding and reasoning.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Image-text multiple-choice questions in a standard setting (text + image) and a vision-only setting where question, options and image are embedded in a single screenshot or photo.
analytical_tasks_explanation: College-level multiple-choice questions requiring subject knowledge and reasoning over diagrams, charts, photos, etc.; vision-only setting additionally requires reading embedded text (OCR) and integrating it with visual content. Paper describes 'multimodal understanding and reasoning'.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Broad multi-discipline benchmark spanning 30 subjects across six disciplines.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Qwen2-VL, InternVL2, LLaVA-OneVision/NeXT, VILA, Pixtral, MiniCPM-V, Phi-3.5-Vision, Idefics3.

quantitative_metrics.note: Accuracy; OCR accuracy via Levenshtein similarity.

summary: MMMU-Pro is a more robust version of MMMU built by filtering text-only-answerable questions, expanding options from 4 to 10, and adding a vision-only setting where questions are embedded in screenshots/photos. Model accuracy drops substantially relative to MMMU, and the paper analyzes CoT, OCR prompts and errors.
key_findings: Performance drops 16.8% to 26.9% vs MMMU (Val) across models. GPT-4o (0513) scores 54.0 (10 options) and 49.7 (vision). CoT generally helps but hurts in Art and Design for LLaVA-OV-72B (-17.12%). OCR prompts have minimal effect. Reasoning errors are 46% of GPT-4o vision errors. Estimated human expert 73.0-85.4.
facets_explanation: Questions and answers are inherited from MMMU, which the paper describes as drawn from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks. Added distractor options were generated by GPT-4o, filtered by Claude 3.5, and reviewed by two rounds of human experts. Answers are scored by exact option-letter match. Answering requires subject knowledge beyond the stimulus.
results_explanation: Best 10-option standard score is Claude 3.5 Sonnet 55.0 (headline); GPT-4o (0513) gets 54.0 and 49.7 on vision. Format gap: LLaVA-OneVision-72B is 38.0 (10 opts) vs 24.0 vision and VILA-1.5-40B falls 37.8 vs MMMU (Val); largest 4-to-10 option/vision gaps reported are ~27 points (VILA ∆2 -37.8 vs Val is cross-benchmark, so the 27 points is Qwen2-VL-7B 54.1 vs 27.0 vision). Human estimate: Human Expert (High) 85.4 vs best 55.0 gives 30.4, rounded to 31 as human estimate Medium 80.8 minus 55.0 is 26; the high figure was used. Human performance is approximated from MMMU data, not directly measured.

humanities_role.quote: MMMU-Pro is designed to more accurately and rigorously assess a model’s true multimodal understanding and reasoning capabilities across a wide range of academic disciplines.

dataset_size.quote: Ultimately, we obtain 3,460 questions—1,730 in standard format and 1,730 as screenshots or photos.

evaluation_set_size.quote: Ultimately, we obtain 3,460 questions—1,730 in standard format and 1,730 as screenshots or photos.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: We evaluate the models with both Direct and CoT prompts (as shown in Appendix A), and report the higher ones in the overall results.

gold_source.quote: MMMU consists of 11.5K carefully curated multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: college-level tasks that require subject-specific knowledge and deliberate reasoning

answer_multiplicity.quote: The model is required to answer a multiple-choice question with up to 10 options
